s: Which of the following was Gandhiji's first Satyagraha Movement in India in which he used Civil Disobedience?
x: Champaran Satyagrah of 1917 A.D. was the first Civil Disobedience Movement led by Gandhiji in India. In 1917 A.D., in the Champaran of Bihar, farmers were protesting against having to grow indigo with barely any payment for it from British. On the invitation of Raj Kumar Shukla, Gandhiji went there and started non-violent protest against this, which eventually led to acceptance of the demands of farmers. This was the first victory of Satyagraha in India.

s: After returning from South Africa, Gandhiji launched his first successful Satyagraha in:
x: In 1917, Gandhi led the Champaran Satyagraha in Bihar against the oppressive indigo plantation system (Tinkathia system). It was his first successful experiment with Satyagraha in India.

s: Who among the following Gandhian followers was a teacher by profession?
x: Jivatram Bhagwandas (Acharya) Kripalani was a professor of history at Muzaffarpur College in Bihar when he first met Mahatma Gandhi in 1917 during the Champaran Satyagraha. It was because of his career in education that he earned the title "Acharya" (teacher). He later served as the Principal of the Gujarat Vidyapith, an institution established by Gandhi.

s: Indigo cultivation in India declined by the beginning of the 20 th century because of
o: Peasant resistance to the oppressive conduct of planters
Its unprofitability in the world market because of new inventions
National leaders' opposition to the cultivation of Indigo
x: The decline of indigo cultivation in India in the early 20 th century was primarily driven by the advent of synthetic dyes, particularly synthetic indigo. By the end of the 19 th century, synthetic dyes had become widely available, drastically reducing the demand for natural indigo. Traditionally, indigo was a natural dye extracted from certain plants, and India had been a major producer of indigo for the global market. Synthetic dyes offered cost-effective alternatives and could be produced in larger quantities, making them more attractive to manufacturers. As a result, the market for natural indigo became unprofitable, leading to a decline in its cultivation in India.

x: Rajkumar Shukla, a local indigo cultivator, met Gandhi at the 1916 Lucknow Congress and persuaded him to come to Champaran.

s: Who had opposed the Champaran Satyagraha of Mahatma Gandhi?
x: N.G. Ranga opposed the Champaran Satyagraha of Mahatma Gandhi. While Rabindranath Tagore gave him the title of ‘Mahatma’ during Champaran Satyagraha.

s: After returning from South Africa, Gandhiji launched his first successful Satyagraha in :
x: Gandhi, the exponent of the Satyagraha Movement, staged his first Satyagraha in Champaran, Bihar in 1917 A.D. The poor peasants, the indigo planters of the district, invited Gandhi to come there to see the grievances of the much-exploited peasants. Gandhiji returned from South Africa in 1915 A.D., and in 1917 he launched his first successful Satyagraha in Champaran on the request of Rajkumar Shukla.

s: Who among the following was not the member of Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee?
x: Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee was presided by F.G. Slay. Its members were D.J. Reid, Mahatma Gandhi, L.C. Adami, Raja Harihar Prasad, Narayan Singh, G. Rainny and M.E.L. Tainer.

o: It was connected with the peasants
Dr. Rajendra Prasad and J.B. Kripalani co-operated
It was the first movement launched by M.K. Gandhi
x: Champaran Satyagraha was limited to Champaran only. The first Movement started by Gandhi at the National level was Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919 A.D.). First three options are correct regarding Champaran Satyagrah.

s: Who was the National Leader of Champaran Indigo movement?
x: The national leader of Champaran Indigo Movement was Mahatma Gandhi.

s: In which of the following Satyagraha movements, did Gandhiji not participate directly?
x: Gandhi did not participate in Vaikom Satyagraha directly. While Rajkot Satyagraha, Kheda, Satyagraha, and Non-cooperation Movement were led by Gandhi. He agreed to settle an agreement with the ruler of Rajkot by mediation with Viceroy after 4 days hunger strike in reference of Rajkot Satyagraha.

s: Who drew Gandhiji's attention to the plight of indigo peasants in Champaran?
x: Rajkumar Shukla, a local indigo cultivator, met Gandhi at the 1916 Lucknow Congress and persuaded him to come to Champaran. Rajendra Prasad and the others were lawyers/associates who joined later.

s: The system of ‘Tinkathia’ in the district of Champaran meant:
o: Cultivation of Indigo by the peasant on 3/20 part of
Cultivation of Indigo by the peasants on 3/21 part of
Cultivation of Indigo by the peasants on 3/19 part of
x: Under the Tinkathia system tenants had to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land for European planters, so option 1 is correct.

s: The person not connected with Champaran movement was-
x: Jai Prakash Narayan was not associated with Champaran Movement, while other names given in options were associated with Champaran Movement.

s: Who amongst the following invited Mahatma Gandhi to Champaran in connection with indigo cultivation?
x: Raj Kumar Shukla, an indigo cultivator, persuaded and invited Mahatma Gandhi to Champaran in relation to indigo cultivation. Gandhi arrived in Champaran on 10th April 1917 with eminent lawyers Brajkishore, Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha, Acharya Kriplani and others.

s: Gandhiji started his first Satyagraha against:
o: Payment of low wages to workers
x: Gandhi launched his first Satyagraha on Indian soil in 1917 A.D.at Champaran, taking up the cause of the poor disinherited peasants and humbled the might of the British and proved to the world that Satyagraha in South Africa was not a fluke, a one-time wonder, but a powerful way of conflict resolution. In February-March 1918 A.D. on the issue of Plague Bonus of labour of Ahmedabad cotton Mill on Strike Gandhi joined the strike and first time he started the hunger strike. In the above question, the Champaran Satyagraha is not given in the option hence Ahmedabad Satyagraha is considered as a correct option.

s: Who among the, following Gandhian followers was a teacher by profession?
x: J.B. Kripalani was basically a teacher by profession among the Gandhian followers. Although Rajendra Prashad also became a teacher for some time, but basically he was a Lawyer.

s: Tinkathia System in Champaran meant:
o: Cultivation of Indigo on the 3/20 area of land
Cultivation of Indigo on 3/19 area of land
Cultivation of Indigo on 3/18 area of land
x: The story of Champaran began in the early 19th century when European planters had involved the cultivators in agreements that forced them to cultivate Indigo on 3/20th of their land (Tinkathia System).Towards the end of 19th century, German synthetic dyes forced Indigo out of the market and the European planters of Champaran, to remove the obligation of cultivating Indigo on the cultivators tried to secure enhancements in rents and other illegal dues as a price for the release. Resistance had surfaced in 1908, but momentum came when Rajkumar Shukla ( a local man) decided to follow Gandhiji and persuaded him to come to Champaran and investigate the problem.

s: During the Champaran Satyagraha, the cultivation of Indigo was known as _________.
x: During the Champaran Satyagrah, the cultivation of Indigo was known as Tinkathia system. Tinkathia was the most prevalent system in Champaran. According to it, the factory owners convinced the tenant to grow indigo in a specific area of his holding for which a fixed price was paid. In this, the ryot was under an obligation to cultivate three kathas per beegha of his land with indigo i.e. 3/20th of his land holding.

s: Those who joined Mahatma Gandhi during the Champaran Satyagraha included:
o: Vallabh Bhai Patel and Vinoba Bhave
Rajendra Prasad and Anugraha Narain Sinha
x: Gandhi reached Champaran with Brajkishore Prasad, Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha and Kripalani, who were Bihar lawyers/associates. Patel, Nehru, Vinoba and Maniben are not listed among them, and Mahadev Desai joined later in 1917 without Maniben.

Indian Government and Anugraha Narayan Singh
x: The Champaran Agrarian Committee was appointed by the Bihar and Orissa government by agreement between the Government and Gandhiji, so option 1 is correct.

Active involvement of Dalit and Tribal communities
Joining of peasant unrest to India’s National
Drastic decrease in the cultivation of plantation crops
x: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was the first Satyagraha of Mahatma Gandhi. One of the very significant aspects of the Champaran Satyagraha was drastic decrease in the cultivation of Plantation crops and commercial crops.

o: The Security of the rights of Harijans
Maintaining of unity of Hindu Society
Solving the problems of Indigo workers

x: Tinkathia was the system in Champaran under which tenants had to grow indigo (neel) on 3/20th of their land for European planters.

s:
Consider the following statements with regard to Champaran Satyagraha (1917).

I. The Champaran Satyagraha marked Mahatma Gandhi’s first appearance in Indian politics as a leader of the masses.

II. Young nationalists like Rajendra Prasad and JB Kripalani had worked with Mahatma Gandhi at Champaran.

III. It was during this movement that Mahatma Gandhi formulated his philosophy of Satyagraha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Champaran was the first satyagraha in India and Rajendra Prasad and Kripalani worked with Gandhi there, so I and II are correct. Statement III is wrong because Satyagraha was already formulated in South Africa.

s: Which one of the following is a very significant aspect of Champaran Satyagraha?
o: Active all India participation of lawyers, students and women in the National Movement
Active involvement of Dalit and Tribal communities of India in the National Movement.
Joining of Peasant urest to India’s National Movement.
Drastic decrease in the cultivation of plantation crops and commercial crops.
x: Champaran connected peasant grievances (indigo cultivators) with Gandhi and the national movement, which is its significant aspect. It did not involve all-India participation of lawyers, students and women, and the decrease in plantation crops was a result.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Dr Rajendra Prasad persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to come to Champaran to investigate the problem of peasants.

II. Acharya JB Kripalani was one of Mahatma Gandhi’s colleagues in his Champaran investigation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rajkumar Shukla, not Rajendra Prasad, persuaded Gandhi to come to Champaran, so I is wrong. J.B. Kripalani accompanied Gandhi there, so II is correct.

s:
Which of the statements given below about the Champaran Satyagraha is/are correct?

I. It was related to Indigo plantations.

II. It started because the European planters oppressed the Zamindars.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: The Champaran struggle was against forced indigo cultivation and illegal exactions by European planters, on behalf of the tenant cultivators. So I is correct. II is wrong because the planters oppressed the tenants, not the zamindars.

s:
Consider the following statements

I. The Champaran Satyagraha marked Gandhiji’s second appearance in Indian politics as a leader of the masses.

II. The Champaran Satyagraha was launched to address the problems faced by Indigo plantation workers.

x: Champaran was launched to solve the problems of indigo workers, so II is correct. It was a localised movement; Gandhi's first all-India venture was the Rowlatt Satyagraha, so I is wrong.

s: Who is not related to the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 AD?
x: Ram Manohar Lohia is not connected with Champaran. Kripalani, Rajkumar Shukla and Rajendra Prasad were all involved.

s: Which event is regarded as the precursor to the Champaran indigo movement?
x: The Bengal Indigo Revolt of 1859 preceded and served as an important precursor to the later indigo-related mobilisation in Champaran.

s: What did the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 abolish?
x: Based on the Enquiry Committee's recommendations, the Act abolished Tinkathia and secured a 25 per cent refund of illegal exactions.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Champaran is incorrect?
o: Plantation owners increased taxes on peasants.
Plantation owners imposed other illegal exactions on peasants.
The issue was connected with indigo exploitation.
Peasants were relieved because plantation owners reduced all taxes voluntarily.
x: Option D is incorrect: the Champaran planters raised taxes and imposed illegal levies; they did not reduce them. The issue arose from forced indigo cultivation.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gandhi’s method during the Champaran Satyagraha?
o: He began an armed resistance against the European planters.
He accepted the order to leave the district and confined his work to petitions.
He called upon peasants to stop cultivating all food crops.
He defied the order to leave and, with his lawyers, recorded peasants’ complaints in the villages.
x: Gandhi defied the official order to leave Champaran and toured villages with his lawyers to record complaints against forced indigo cultivation. This compelled the government to order an inquiry.

s: Who chaired the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee (1917), on which Gandhi represented the ryots?
x: F.G. Sly chaired the committee, appointed by the Bihar and Orissa government.

s: Against what was the Champaran Satyagraha mainly directed?
o: Forced indigo cultivation and illegal exactions by European planters
x: European planters compelled peasants to grow indigo and, when indigo became unprofitable, demanded illegal dues and enhanced rents; forest tax was not the issue.

s: What did 'tawan' mean in Champaran?
o: Lump-sum compensation demanded when indigo lost its value
x: Tawan was lump-sum compensation extracted when indigo became less valuable; sharahbeshi was enhanced rent.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in the context of Champaran?
o: Mahadev Desai — Leader of the European planters
x: Mahadev Desai was Gandhi’s secretary and pledged himself to the Champaran work in 1917. He was not a leader of the European planters.

s: What was the occupation of Rajkumar Shukla, who persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to visit Champaran?
o: Lawyer of the Bihar High Court
x: Rajkumar Shukla was a local indigo cultivator and agriculturist of Champaran who persuaded Gandhi to investigate the peasants’ condition. Rajendra Prasad was an associate, not the inviter.

s: On which date did Gandhi reach Champaran?
x: Gandhi reached Champaran on 10 April 1917 with Brajkishore Prasad, Rajendra Prasad and others.

s: What did 'Sharahbeshi' mean in Champaran?
x: Sharahbeshi was enhanced rent; tawan was lump-sum compensation and tinkathia the 3/20th indigo obligation.

s: By whose agreement was the Champaran Agrarian Committee of 1917 appointed?
o: The Viceroy and the Secretary of State
x: The Bihar and Orissa government appointed the Champaran Agrarian Committee by agreement with Gandhiji, who sat on it for the ryots.

s: Who is the author of 'Mahatma Gandhi and Bihar, Some Reminiscences'?

s: Which of the following books was written by Dr. Rajendra Prasad?
o: Mahatma Gandhi and Bihar, Some Reminiscences
x: Rajendra Prasad wrote 'Mahatma Gandhi and Bihar, Some Reminiscences'; India Wins Freedom is by Azad, The Discovery of India by Nehru, Gandhi and Anarchy by Sankaran Nair.

s: What share of the illegal charges was refunded to the peasants under the Champaran settlement?
x: The Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918 abolished Tinkathia and refunded 25% of the illegal charges.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918:
1. It abolished the Tinkathia system.
2. It refunded 50 per cent of the illegal dues collected by planters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Act abolished Tinkathia but the refund was 25%, not 50%.

s: Why had indigo become unprofitable for the European planters of Champaran by the early 20th century?
o: The British banned the export of indigo
German synthetic dyes replaced natural indigo in the world market
The Champaran Agrarian Act fixed low prices
x: German synthetic dyes made indigo unprofitable; planters then raised rents and imposed illegal dues on tenants.

s: Identify below the cause of the dispute between mill owners and workers, which led to the mill workers strike in 1917 at Ahmedabad.
x: The Ahmedabad mill owners withdrew the plague bonus, which triggered the dispute and the strike.

s: Who participated in ‘Satyagraha’ started by Gandhiji at Ahmedabad in 1917-18?
x: The Ahmedabad struggle involved mill workers, i.e. industrial labour, unlike the peasant movements of Champaran and Kheda.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918.

I. It was related to a dispute between the workers and the European mill owners regarding hours of work.

II. Gandhiji advised the workers to go on strike.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The dispute was over the plague bonus and wages, not hours of work, and the mill owners were led by Ambalal Sarabhai, an Indian, not European owners. So I is wrong. Gandhi did advise the workers on the strike, so II is correct.

s: Which among the following stuggles, based on Gandhi’s philosophy of Satyagraha, involved the industrial working class?
x: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike involved mill workers, i.e. the industrial working class. Champaran and Kheda were peasant struggles.

s: Which of the following struggles of Mahatma Gandhi was related to industrial workers?
x: The Ahmedabad Satyagraha was the struggle of mill workers, i.e. industrial labour. Champaran and Kheda concerned peasants.

s: In the Ahmedabad Mill Strike, what were the workers' demand and the mill owners' offer, respectively?
o: 20 per cent wage increase and 35 per cent increase
50 per cent wage increase and 20 per cent increase
35 per cent wage increase and 50 per cent increase
50 per cent wage increase and complete withdrawal of wages
x: The workers demanded a 50 per cent wage increase because of wartime inflation, while the mill owners offered only 20 per cent.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike took place in 1918.
Workers received a 35% bonus after the result of the strike.
The dispute involved plague bonus and wages.
x: Option C is incorrect: the 1918 Ahmedabad Mill Strike lasted 21 days, not 35. It concerned the plague bonus and wages, and the workers won a 35 per cent increase.

s: Who founded the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association, also known as Majoor Mahajan Sangh, in 1920?
o: Ambalal Sarabhai with Vallabhbhai Patel's guidance
J.B. Kripalani with Anugrah Narayan Sinha's guidance
x: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association (Majoor Mahajan Sangh) was founded by Gandhi with Anusuya Sarabhai on 25 February 1920; it worked through arbitration and non-violence.

s: What wage rise did the tribunal award the workers in the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918)?
x: The workers had demanded 50%; Gandhi advised 35% and the tribunal awarded 35%.

s: Who led the mill owners in the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918)?
x: Ambalal Sarabhai led the mill owners; his sister Anusuya Sarabhai stood with the workers.

s: How long did the Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918 last?
x: The strike lasted 21 days, not 35; 35% was the wage rise awarded.

s: The withdrawal of which allowance by the mill owners led to the Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918?
x: The Ahmedabad mill owners withdrew the plague bonus, and the workers demanded a 50% wage rise instead.

s: Who among the following first took up the cause of the Ahmedabad mill workers and appealed to Gandhi in 1918?
x: The workers approached Anusuya Sarabhai, who appealed to Gandhi; her brother Ambalal Sarabhai led the mill owners.

s: The first venture of Gandhi in all India politics was the:
x: Champaran (1917), Kheda (1918), Ahmedabad (1918) — were localised movements addressing peasants' and workers' grievances. The Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919), against the repressive Rowlatt Act, was Gandhi's first all-India political campaign. He organised the Satyagraha Sabha and called for a nationwide hartal on April 6, 1919, marking his emergence as a national leader. The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920) was larger in scale but came later, not as his first venture into all-India politics.

s: The first venture of Gandhi in all-India politics was the:
x: Every movement started by Gandhiji helped Indian Nationalism to attain an unprecedented height. The Movements conceived by Gandhiji like Champaran Peasant Movement (1917 A.D.), Ahmedabad Mill Workers Movement (1918 A.D.), Kheda Peasant Movement(1918 A.D.) were limited to the specific issue of a particular section of the society. The scope of the area was also very limited. But Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919 A.D.) against the censure of freedom of press and detention without trial was proactively joined by all the sections of the society. Sentiments of the aggrieved common people were addressed. Knitting of people from all religions, all castes, all age groups, and both the genders in the Nationalist Movement had a distinguished characteristic of the Rowlatt Satyagraha. National newspapers, political journals, etc. made Gandhi a popular figure. This was the first all India level Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi.

s: Where did Gandhi form the Satyagraha Sabha against the Rowlatt Act on 24 February 1919?

s: Under the Rowlatt Act, for how long could political suspects be detained without trial?

s:

x: Dyer blocked the only exit and fired without warning for about 10 minutes on the crowd gathered in the garden, and he was the officer who ordered the firing. So I, II and III are all correct.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the firing at Jallianwala Bagh is NOT correct?

The crowd was given a clear warning and sufficient time to disperse before firing began.
x: Statement D is NOT correct: Dyer gave no warning and no time to disperse. He blocked the only exit of the walled garden and fired without warning for about ten minutes, using 1,650 rounds, so A, B and C are correct.

s: According to official figures, what were the casualties in the Jallianwala Bagh firing?
x: The official figures recorded 379 deaths and 1,100 injuries, although the Indian National Congress estimated a higher death toll.

s: After the Hunter Committee condemned General Dyer's conduct, which body backed him?
x: The Hunter Committee, appointed after the massacre, condemned Dyer, but the House of Lords supported him.

s: At Jallianwala Bagh, Dyer's troops fired about how many rounds in some 10 minutes?
x: About 1,650 rounds were fired in around 10 minutes; 379 dead and 1,100 injured were the official figures.
